title: The search after the search
styleLine: ONE CONSISTENT LINE ACROSS ALL IMAGES (critical). Cinematic editorial photography, shot as if by the SAME photographer on the SAME 35mm lens, same warm natural grade — deep navy shadows (#262B38) + warm cream light (#F7F8EA), rich but natural (NOT a heavy Instagram filter, NOT washed-out, NOT HDR). Modern boutique-hotel world: walnut wood, cream plaster, greenery, contemporary fixtures. NO dated props (no key racks, service bells, fountain pens, paper ledgers, cash). Elegant, quiet, expensive. 4:5 aspect (1080x1350), designed for Instagram feed carousels (full frame visible) and TikTok photo carousels. SAFE ZONES: (a) Instagram profile grid crops to CENTER 1:1 — the top ~135px and bottom ~135px are cropped in the grid view, so keep the hero subject center-frame. (b) TikTok photo mode overlays a caption/UI region across the bottom ~340px on the visible feed — keep any critical visual detail above that band. (c) The lower ~40% of the frame (roughly y=810 to y=1350 on a 1080x1350 canvas) is reserved for on-slide type — compose the subject in the upper ~55-60% but fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area. A CSS gradient handles text legibility. No text, no logos, no clearly identifiable faces.
note: Path C. Slides 1 and 4 are frameless composites — clean editorial scenes with UI screenshots overlaid freely (no devices, no frames, no white panels). Remaining slides are pure editorial photos. Companion to scene-13.

slides.imagePrompt: A warm boutique-hotel lobby interior: cream plaster walls, a walnut console table with a coffee cup and a small potted fern, warm natural side light filtering through sheer curtains, a leather accent chair. The composition leaves generous open space in the upper-center of the frame — an airy, uncluttered wall area with soft light. NO DEVICE, NO SCREEN, NO FRAME, NO MONITOR, NO DISPLAY PANEL — just the pure editorial scene. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.headline:
The search
==after the search==.
slides.sub: How Booking becomes your ad budget. Without you paying for a click.

slides.title: The ==first search== isn't yours
slides.body: The guest types 'boutique hotel Vancouver' into Booking. They see twenty properties. Yours is one of them. So far, so ordinary.

slides.imagePrompt: A single printed photograph or open magazine on a walnut coffee table, showing a warm hotel interior detail — walnut, plant, sheer curtain. No readable text, no branding. Warm indirect light. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. slides.title: They ==stop== on you
slides.body: One of the photos catches their eye. Or the location. Or the room description. They tap in, read reviews, look at rates. Twenty seconds of real attention.

slides.imagePrompt: REUSE s1.png — same frameless scene image as slide 1.
slides.title: Then they open a ==new tab==
slides.body: They Google your name. Not 'boutique hotel Vancouver,' your name. This is the moment Booking paid to introduce you. It's also the moment their job is done.

slides.title: Your site has ==one job== now
slides.body: Close the guest that Booking already warmed up. Same rate, better perks (free cancellation, room upgrade, breakfast). One clear button. That's the whole game.
